problem_type: A plan edit action available to the user is outside the current visible view or behind an irrelevant disclosure.
symptom: A zero-card storyboard advertised Add reference behind Expand all, and Add shot fell below the fixed footer.
direct_cause: Both controls were subordinate to data presentation: the first depended on expanded rows and the second was the last scrolling child.
class_root: The editor did not give its persistent and empty-state edit actions a visible entry independent of whether their target rows were visible.
affected_population: Creators editing a storyboard whose shots extend below the visible viewport
entry_points: Manual append from the production plan editor footer

external_sources.purpose: Scroll an existing row to the closest visible position.
Keep virtualization with the existing table owner.

invariants: The editable zero-card state offers one Add reference button and no expand/collapse control. Adding creates an editable row.
The production editor offers one Add shot button outside its scrolling content, using the existing plan mutator. A new shot is revealed through its row or the existing virtual row navigation.

door_reduction.why_not: The production editor owns plan writes. Lab callers exercise the same existing presentation at independently signed states. The two plan mutators create different domain records.

generality_proof: The zero-card rule depends on card count for every render configuration. The add-shot control sits outside the scroll container regardless of its height, while navigation remains with the existing virtualized table when the row has not mounted.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the empty/populated split and the first add action.
Route footer append to the active plan and reveal its new row.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The interaction regression checks immediate editing and the transition to normal disclosure.
The interaction regression opens a plan larger than its viewport, appends from the footer and reads the resulting viewport and shot.

recurrence.reason: Every newly opened zero-reference plan or sufficiently tall shot table can reach the same UI conditions.
same_class_scan: door-map results in the design card for zone, footer, addAnchor and addShot
Exact accessible-name consumers in original-storyboard-editor.test.mjs, _storyboardAgentBulkSteps.mjs and storyboard-windowing.walk.mjs

prevention.invariant: An available local edit has a visible entry from its initial state, and adding a row uses the existing plan owner.
prevention.failure_mode: An empty zone offers no disclosure. Plans still pass the existing store write rules.
prevention.strategy: Place the one append action in the persistent footer and bind the empty-zone action to the explicit create event.

legacy_paths.rationale: Replace the dashed end-of-scroll append and remove the zero-card disclosure state.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Presentation is owned by Nomi. Existing browser and virtualizer APIs already supply the required navigation.

migration: Existing projects, plans and accessible names require no migration.
residual_risks: Existing walk entry points that rely on a paid provider were not used for this zero-spend UI flow.
The existing draft-save walkthrough setup requires the old disclosure on its zero-card fixture. The test file is outside the requested scope.
